messages.content: You write the short explanations that first-year programming students in India type when a C quiz asks them "Why did you choose that answer?". Reply with a JSON object only.

A student was shown this C code and question.

Code:
int p;
for (i = 1; i <= 3; i++) { p = 1; p = p * 2; }

Question: What is p after the loop?
The student answered: 8

The student holds this wrong belief and does not know it is wrong: The total keeps its value across passes even if it is set again inside the loop

Write 5 different explanations this student might type for why they chose that answer.
Voice: sure of themselves, plain English, one sentence of 8 to 18 words.

Rules:
- Each one must show the student's reasoning, not just repeat the answer.
- Write as the student, in the first person or with no subject. Do not judge the answer or say it is wrong.
- Do not name the idea as a rule and do not use textbook terms for the mistake.
- Make the 5 explanations differ in wording and in which part of the code they point at.

Return JSON: {"sentences": ["...", "..."]}

content: {"sentences": ["The value keeps adding up each time the loop runs, so 1 times 2 three times gives 8.", "Every pass doubles whatever total I already have from before, so 2 becomes 4 then 8.", "Since p is set to 1 but the loop runs three times, the multiplication stacks up to 8.", "The loop repeats three times and each repeat doubles the number, ending at 8.", "I multiplied 2 by itself three times because there are three rounds of the loop, giving 8."]}

sentences: The value keeps adding up each time the loop runs, so 1 times 2 three times gives 8.
Every pass doubles whatever total I already have from before, so 2 becomes 4 then 8.
Since p is set to 1 but the loop runs three times, the multiplication stacks up to 8.
The loop repeats three times and each repeat doubles the number, ending at 8.
I multiplied 2 by itself three times because there are three rounds of the loop, giving 8.
